name: @anclora/design-system
_agentReadme: This manifest is the machine-readable contract for coding agents working in any Anclora repo. Read componentStatus before adding a component (canonical = consume it, do not rebuild it; candidate = usable but not yet a hard requirement; needsConsumerEvidence = ships but has no confirmed real usage, verify before relying on it). Read profiles before choosing shell/density defaults for a new app. Read extensionPoints before overriding anything — if the property you need to change is not listed as a component's extension point, add a variant here instead of overriding the base selector. Read prohibitedPatterns before writing CSS that touches an .ac-* selector directly. Read theme before implementing light/dark in any new app — as of 0.7.0 the package ships a real canonical light theme, do not invent a local one. Read borders before deciding which border token to use — not every border needs 3:1, but a control/status border does, and there's a specific token for that. Full architecture: ANCLORA-DESIGN-SYSTEM-ARCHITECTURE.md. Full theme contract: docs/themes/light-dark-theme-contract.md. Full border/status/link contract: docs/tokens/semantic-borders-and-status.md. Full evidence: docs/ecosystem-audit/.

subtle.guarantee: none — may be low contrast, decorative only
subtle.use: row dividers, section rules, anywhere the surface stays identifiable without the border

control.guarantee: WCAG 2.2 non-text >=3:1 against the surface it's painted on, verified against Core's own surfaces AND a real product surface fixture
control.use: form inputs/selects/textareas, and any future component where the border is the primary/only cue that something is a control or panel boundary

status.guarantee: >=3:1 against the badge's own surface, verified per tone per theme
status.use: ONLY .ac-status-badge — do not invent a local status border color; if a tone the DS doesn't cover is needed, that's Design System feedback, not a local addition

borders.rule: WCAG 2.2 non-text contrast (1.4.11) applies when a border is necessary to perceive the component or its state — not to every visible line. A Modal's border, where elevation/shadow/backdrop already define the boundary, can stay on --border-default (unguaranteed). An input field's border, with no other strong boundary cue, needs --border-control. When genuinely unsure, prefer --border-control over silently relying on --border-default's unguaranteed contrast.
borders.note: --border-default/--border are unchanged in 0.8.0 (still decorative-strength, not retroactively strengthened) — --border-control is additive specifically so ~30 existing consumers that never asked for a stronger default aren't visually changed. Full rationale, evidence, and the exact contrast numbers: docs/tokens/semantic-borders-and-status.md.

linkText.rule: A product accent valid for fills/icons/decoration is not automatically valid as normal-size text — 3:1 (non-text) and 4.5:1 (text) are different requirements, and an accent's contrast against its own canvas varies by product and by theme.
linkText.darkFormula: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 80%, white 20%) — fixed in 0.8.0, was var(--accent) raw (Command Center's real accent measured 4.34:1 there, below the 4.5:1 AA text minimum)
linkText.lightFormula: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 45%, black 55%) — unchanged since 0.7.0
linkText.prohibited: Using --accent (or any raw product accent) directly as --text-link, or as any normal-size text color, without verifying contrast against the actual canvas it will render on.

theme.defaultBehavior: No data-theme attribute set -> :root values apply, which are identical to [data-theme="dark"] (backward compatible with every pre-0.7.0 consumer).
dsOwns: visual theme semantics per role (--bg, --text-primary, --status-danger-text, etc.)
WCAG 2.2 AA contrast for every semantic text/surface pair it defines
appOwns: SSR-safe pre-hydration script that sets data-theme before first paint
mustNotRedefine: the meaning of a semantic role (e.g. what counts as 'danger')
--focus-ring or any accessibility-load-bearing token, for aesthetic reasons
theme.brandVsTheme: --accent (and other .product-anclora-* brand tokens in themes/product.css) is theme-invariant — the same brand color is used in both dark and light. Only its DERIVED usages (--text-link, --focus-ring, --text-on-accent) are recomputed per theme, because a brand accent that passes contrast in dark mode can fail it in light mode (verified: Core's own silver accent is 2.04:1 as raw text on the light canvas, fails AA; darkened via color-mix it's 7.62:1).

answersForAgents.I need light/dark theme for a new Anclor: No. Set data-theme="dark"|"light" on <html> and consume the canonical semantic tokens from tokens/semantic.css — do not copy a token block from anclora-talent or anclora-command-center, and do not invent your own selector/class/attribute for theme.
answersForAgents.Can I set a custom brand accent while st: Yes — that's what themes/product.css's .product-anclora-* layer is for. Override --accent (and, only if your brand identity genuinely requires it, --bg/--fg*) there; do not touch the semantic role definitions in tokens/semantic.css itself.

categories.FOUNDATION: Raw scales, brand primitives and platform-independent building blocks.
categories.SEMANTIC: Theme-aware meaning such as surfaces, text, focus, borders and status roles.
categories.PROFILE: Structural/compositional values for Core/default, P-WKS and P-MKT.
categories.PRODUCT_EXTENSION_POINT: Documented product identity or composition values; never a replacement for semantic meaning.

externalReferences.--layer-sticky: Optional consumer cascade override with a fallback in app-shell.css.
externalReferences.--layer-skip-link: Optional consumer cascade override with a fallback in app-shell.css.
externalReferences.--ac-stat-columns: Optional stat-strip composition override with a fallback.
externalReferences.--stack-gap: Optional primitive composition override with a fallback.
externalReferences.--cluster-gap: Optional primitive composition override with a fallback.

tokenOwnership.rule: Every executable Design System token is defined once in the canonical package or explicitly classified as an optional external extension with a fallback. Product extensions may not redefine semantic roles, focus, generic anatomy or state meaning.

forms.architecture: Field owns label/hint/message relationships; Control owns value/focus/disabled/readonly/invalid state.
forms.requiredSemantics: Use required or aria-required on the actual control; visible asterisk is supplemental only.
forms.errorSemantics: Use aria-invalid=true and aria-describedby for the visible error message; never rely on color alone.
forms.disabledVsReadonly: disabled is unavailable and not submitted; readonly text remains focusable, readable and submitted.

combobox.rule: Do not promote a shared combobox until two materially different consumers validate the API and keyboard model.

extensionPoints: field density only where a sanctioned variant exists
prohibitedPatterns: placeholder-only labels
color-only errors
clickable div controls without native semantics
consumer-local focus rings or control borders
premature shared combobox abstraction

layers.primitives: native table semantics: caption, thead, tbody, tr, th and td
layers.behaviours: compose sorting, selection, filters, pagination and bulk actions; application owns state

dataTable.defaultResponsiveStrategy: horizontal overflow for simple tables; documented mobile list/card transformation for action-heavy tables
dataTable.sorting: native button inside th plus aria-sort; no sorting engine
dataTable.selection: application-owned state using canonical Forms checkbox; data-selected is presentation only
dataTable.rowActions: compose ac-button, including ac-button--icon only with an accessible name
dataTable.pagination: separate application composition; no table-owned pagination component
dataTable.sticky: opt-in via ac-data-table--sticky; sticky columns are not supported
prohibitedPatterns: MegaDataTable
data-fetching table wrapper
generic sorting engine
local table-action-button
inline spreadsheet editing
virtualisation
column resize
pinned columns
drag reorder

answersForAgents.I need to display records: Use the canonical native table contract and .ac-data-table; do not create a local table family.
answersForAgents.I need row actions: Compose the canonical Button/link/menu semantics; do not create .table-action-button or .row-menu-button.
answersForAgents.I need filters: Compose canonical Forms outside the table; the table does not own filter controls.
answersForAgents.I need an editable spreadsheet-like grid: Do not force Data Table; classify as DATA_GRID_EVIDENCE_REQUIRED.
answersForAgents.I need mobile: Use horizontal overflow for simple tables; use a documented accessible list/card composition for action-heavy tables.

feedback.architecture: Separate persistent alerts, transient toasts, full-surface empty/error states, short-lived loading, determinate progress, operation processing and structural skeleton placeholders. No generic mega-feedback component.
feedback.runtimeOwnership: The Design System owns anatomy, tokens and semantic guidance. Each product owns data fetching, queues, timers, portals, retry logic and live-region timing.
feedback.ariaGuidance: Use role=status for polite progress/loading updates and role=alert only for urgent dynamic errors. A static informational alert may have no live role. Progress exposes min/max/value when determinate; indeterminate progress must not fake a value.

answersForAgents.an API request failed for the page: Use Error State with a recovery action.
answersForAgents.a field is invalid: Use the Forms field message with aria-invalid and aria-describedby.
answersForAgents.an operation succeeded: Use Toast or an in-context confirmation; do not use a full-page error/success state.
answersForAgents.an import or export is running: Use Loading for unknown duration, Progress for a trustworthy numeric value, and Processing when the operation has meaningful activity context.
answersForAgents.there are no records: Use Empty State; distinguish first-use, no-results, filtered and permission variants through content and product-owned context.

sharedPatterns.implementation: CSS-first composition classes; application owns runtime, state, data, permissions and business rules
promotionCriteria: recurs in at least 2 independent products
same semantic purpose and compatible lifecycle
responsive behaviour is stable at mobile, tablet and desktop
ES/EN copy expansion does not break the composition

answersForAgents.I need login: Compose auth-entry; authentication provider, session and redirect logic remain in the application.
answersForAgents.I need settings: Compose settings-section; available settings and persistence remain in the application.
answersForAgents.I need upload and processing: Separate file-upload from processing-result; do not build a domain-specific transfer component.
answersForAgents.I need delete confirmation: Compose destructive-confirmation with the canonical Modal; the mutation remains application-owned.
answersForAgents.I need filters above a dataset: Check filter-toolbar evidence first; Wave 8 keeps it a candidate until a stable cross-product lifecycle is proven.
answersForAgents.I need employee onboarding: No canonical onboarding pattern exists; keep the workflow product-specific unless new evidence satisfies promotion criteria.

adoptionStages.NOT_ADOPTED: No runtime dependency or public Design System import verified.
adoptionStages.FOUNDATIONS: At least one public token, foundation or theme entrypoint is imported at runtime.
adoptionStages.COMPONENTS: At least one public component family is imported and composed at runtime.
adoptionStages.SHELL_PROFILE: The consumer composes a canonical profile or shell contract at runtime.
adoptionStages.PATTERNS: A shared product pattern is composed in a real workflow; runtime validation may still be partial.
adoptionStages.SUBSTANTIAL: Multiple canonical layers are consumed across a meaningful product surface.

adoptionContract.referenceConsumerDefinition: Validated implementation evidence or useful integration example; never the source of truth and not an adoption stage.

profileScope.declaration: data-profile on the application or route layout root
profileScope.mixedArchetypeRule: A repository may contain multiple route/layout roots with different profiles. Do not nest competing data-profile declarations; the nearest sanctioned layout root owns the surface.
profileScope.themeIndependence: data-theme is independent from data-profile. A single-theme consumer may omit a theme switch while consuming canonical semantic roles.

dependencyPolicy.canonical: Pin the immutable V1 Git SHA for reproducible adoption.
dependencyPolicy.currentDistribution: private GitHub SHA tarball; registry publication is a post-v1 governance candidate
dependencyPolicy.supportedOlder: A consumer may remain on an older immutable SHA while its imported public paths remain supported and the migration gap is recorded.

cssImportContract.granular: Public exports under tokens/*, taxonomy/*, themes/*, foundations/*, components/* and patterns/shared-product-patterns.css.
cssImportContract.consumerBridge: If a bundler cannot resolve nested CSS imports from an external package, a documented granular-import bridge is allowed; do not copy token or component CSS without recording the bridge.
cssImportContract.sideEffects: CSS entrypoints are package side effects and are declared in package.json.

adoptionContract.headlessPolicy: Radix, Base UI, shadcn and other headless runtimes may remain implementation details for focus, keyboard, portals and positioning. The .ac-* contract remains the visual authority.
adoptionContract.extensionPolicy: Product copy, branding accents, composition and documented profile behaviour may extend the system. Semantic roles, focus, generic anatomy and state meaning may not be redefined locally.

deprecationPolicy.marker: Add a manifest deprecated entry and documentation marker with replacement, since, reason and removal condition.
deprecationPolicy.warningPeriod: At least one compatible release before removal in pre-v1; breaking removals require an explicit version/release note.

qaPolicy.consumerMigration: One coherent surface per wave, followed by real-browser responsive, i18n and accessibility validation.
qaPolicy.destructiveE2E: Fail closed against production-backed consumers; use dedicated non-production QA or service credentials and ignored artifacts.
qaPolicy.referenceConsumersAreNotAuthority: Inspect reference consumers for evidence only; canonical executable truth remains this repository.

doesNotBlockV1: unimplemented Command Palette, Combobox or Data Grid without blocking evidence
postV1Candidates: registry distribution after release governance exists
consumerMigrationOnly: consumer-specific theme and headless runtime adapters

overlays.architecture: CSS visual contract plus semantic HTML and an optional consumer-owned accessible runtime. The Design System does not ship a universal Overlay component or mandate Radix.

decisionRules.three contextual actions: Menu, usually opened by an explicit Button/icon-only Button trigger.
decisionRules.short supplemental help: Tooltip on hover and keyboard focus; it is non-interactive and never the only accessible name.
decisionRules.rich contextual controls: Non-modal Popover; the page remains interactive and the panel owns only its contextual content.
decisionRules.mobile side panel: Drawer/Sheet when content is substantial or a desktop contextual surface needs a mobile composition.
decisionRules.searchable options: Combobox contract; currently evidence-required and not a generic Popover.

runtimeOwnership.menu: Consumer-owned or recommended headless primitive; runtime owns roving focus, keyboard navigation, dismissal and focus return.
runtimeOwnership.popover: Consumer-owned or recommended headless primitive; runtime owns positioning, collision handling, focus strategy and dismissal.
runtimeOwnership.tooltip: Consumer-owned or recommended tooltip primitive; runtime owns hover/focus timing and relationship; content remains non-interactive.
runtimeOwnership.drawer: Consumer-owned or recommended dialog/sheet primitive; modal drawers require focus containment and inert/backdrop behaviour.

prohibitedPatterns: MegaOverlay
generic div menu items without keyboard semantics
tooltip used as an icon accessible name
interactive controls inside Tooltip
manual focus trap duplicated per consumer
arbitrary z-index scale
generic Popover used for Combobox or Select semantics
Popover used for blocking confirmation
Modal used for a lightweight command list

maturity.STABLE: Executable contract verified in this repository and supported by real consumer evidence.
maturity.CANONICAL_NEEDS_MORE_RUNTIME_EVIDENCE: Shipped canonical CSS with incomplete independent consumer/runtime evidence; do not describe as battle-tested.
maturity.EVIDENCE_REQUIRED: Not a v1 stable contract; requires a focused audit and consumer validation before promotion.
maturity.DEPRECATED: Supported only for compatibility until its documented removal condition is met.

componentStatus._note: The legacy canonical/needsConsumerEvidence arrays remain as compatibility metadata; the maturity object is the v1 decision surface.

Core.name: Core / default
Core.description: Shared semantic tokens, accessibility, overlays, controls and content primitives. Use when the product has no persistent workspace shell and is not a public narrative marketing surface.

P-MKT.name: Marketing / Landing
P-MKT.description: Public, unauthenticated, single-scroll narrative page. No persistent nav shell.

P-WKS.name: Workspace / Operational
P-WKS.description: Authenticated, persistent sidebar/topbar shell, high information density: tables, entity lists, forms, modals, status badges.
mayOverride: component density/size defaults (use .ac-button--compact, not a new class)

profiles._note: Profile declaration is deterministic: set data-profile="workspace" for P-WKS, data-profile="marketing" for P-MKT, and omit it for Core/default. Full app-to-profile assignment: ANCLORA-DESIGN-SYSTEM-PRODUCT-MATRIX.md.

navigationShell.activeState: consumer supplies aria-current=page on the route link
navigationShell.mobileWorkspaceModel: persistent sidebar becomes modal Drawer below 960px when evidence supports P-WKS
navigationShell.scrollModel: one page/content scroll by default; sidebar and Drawer may scroll independently when content requires it

button.note: --compact (0.5.0) is the canonical 'smaller/denser button for a workspace surface'. --icon (0.6.0) is the canonical square icon-only shape — composes with EVERY variant and EVERY density, all 16 combinations are implemented and technically supported (e.g. `ac-button ac-button--ghost ac-button--icon` or `ac-button ac-button--secondary ac-button--compact ac-button--icon`); it is NOT a separate component, do not build '.icon-button'/'.table-action-button'/'.dashboard-icon-button' locally. Design guidance (not a blocked combination): avoid `--destructive --compact --icon` for a high-consequence action — a small unlabeled icon button is an easy mis-tap target for something irreversible; prefer default (44px) density for destructive icon actions, or add a confirmation step. An icon-only button MUST have an aria-label (or aria-labelledby) — the icon itself is never an accessible name, and a title/tooltip does not substitute for one. Do not use --icon for a toggle control that needs aria-pressed, or for a control that needs a specialized primitive (segmented toggle, etc.) — see prohibitedPatterns.

answersForAgents.I need a square icon-only button: Use `ac-button ac-button--<variant> ac-button--icon` (add `ac-button--compact` for the dense/36px version). Do not create a local class.
answersForAgents.Can I use --destructive --compact --icon: Yes, technically supported — but for a high-consequence/irreversible action prefer the default (44px, non-compact) density instead, since a small unlabeled icon target is an easy mis-tap for something destructive. Not a blocked combination, just guidance.
answersForAgents.Is .ac-button--icon safe against a local: Yes as of 0.6.0 — --icon uses a compound selector (.ac-button.ac-button--icon) specifically hardened against the cascade bug found in the anclora-talent Wave 1 pilot. --compact and the color variants are NOT hardened the same way yet; if this consumer has a local `.ac-button { ... }` override, scope it with :not(.ac-button--compact) etc. — see docs/ecosystem-audit/05-button-contract-hardening.md.

prohibitedPatterns: Inventing a local status border color (e.g. a consumer-specific --status-danger-border) instead of using the canonical --status-*-border tier — added 0.8.0 specifically so consumers stop needing to do this.
Using --accent (or any raw product accent) as normal-size text (including --text-link) without verifying contrast — a fill/icon-safe accent is not automatically text-safe. See linkText.
Using --border-subtle or --border-default where recognizing the component genuinely depends on the border being visible (e.g. a form input) — use --border-control instead.

Globally strengthening --border-subtle or --border-default to fix one component's contrast problem instead of using --border-control on that component — this changes every consumer that never asked for a stronger default.

Overriding border-radius, font-size, font-weight, or text-transform directly on the bare .ac-button selector in a consumer app instead of using a --compact/--sm/--lg/--icon variant or an --ac-button-* custom property.
Building a local icon-only button class ('.icon-button', '.table-action-button', '.dashboard-icon-button', or similar) instead of composing `ac-button ac-button--<variant> ac-button--icon`.
Shipping an .ac-button--icon (or any icon-only control) without an aria-label/aria-labelledby, or relying on a tooltip/title as the accessible name.
Repurposing .ac-button as a toggle/pressed-state control (needs aria-pressed) or a menu/segmented-control primitive it wasn't designed for.

Creating a new parallel button/card/modal class family in a consumer app (e.g. '.app-button', '.dashboard-button') when a canonical .ac-* component with a suitable variant already exists or could exist as one — propose a variant here instead.
Redefining semantic tokens (--status-*, --danger, --success, --warning, --focus-ring) with app-local hex values instead of consuming the semantic layer.
Inventing a new theme-toggle mechanism (a fourth alternative to the data-theme attribute contract) in a new app.
Treating a shadcn/ui-generated component's default HSL/OKLCH palette as final without wiring it to Anclora's semantic/component tokens.
Building a data-fetching MegaDataTable or generic sorting/query engine in the Design System.
Replacing semantic tables with generic div grids without a documented responsive/accessibility reason.
Making every table row clickable or relying on tr onClick without an equivalent keyboard interaction.
Creating table-specific checkbox, select, input, status or pagination variants when canonical primitives compose.
Building a generic MegaFeedback component that merges alert, toast, empty, error, loading and progress semantics.
Using role=alert for every informational message or exposing a fake progress value for indeterminate work.
Replacing an actionable operation indicator with a spinner-only or skeleton-only surface.
Creating a consumer-local status palette, toast queue or notification centre without evidence and a documented contract.
Creating a universal MegaOverlay that merges Menu, Popover, Tooltip, Drawer and Modal semantics.
Using Tooltip for interactive content or as the only accessible name of an icon-only control.
Creating a local filter-toolbar, upload anatomy or destructive-confirmation wrapper when the canonical shared-pattern contract applies.
Copying a product-specific import, onboarding or entity-management workflow into Core as a shared pattern.
Building a monolithic super-pattern component that owns business state, permissions, persistence or API calls.
Using Popover for Combobox/Select semantics or for a blocking confirmation.
Adding consumer-local arbitrary z-index values or duplicating focus traps without a documented runtime need.

deprecated.reason: product rename, alias retained for consumer migration
deprecated.removalCondition: Remove after all supported consumers confirm no legacy token usage and the next breaking release is announced.

deprecated.reason: product rename, alias retained for consumer migration
deprecated.removalCondition: Remove after all supported consumers confirm no legacy selector usage and the next breaking release is announced.

knownGaps.issue: theme-invariant (same black-based value in dark and light) as of 0.7.0 — not redefined per data-theme. Acceptable simplification for now, documented as a scoped-out follow-up, not an oversight.

microsaas.purpose: Focused, recurring SaaS utilities with compact workflows and verifiable results.
microsaas.extensionPolicy: Products may extend accent, copy, density and product data; semantic roles and component anatomy remain canonical.
